text:
maria: Thinking out loud — proposal to support optimistic (speculative) invokes for multi-step tool flows. idea: kick off multiple compatible tool calls in parallel with soft time budgets and let the first successful result win, fall back to ordered retry only if none succeed in budget. want to discuss UX and spec changes.

vikram: I like optimistic invokes for latency-sensitive paths. main questions: how do we express compatibility between tools? and how do we charge customers when we fire 2+ calls? :money_with_wings:

laura: Compatibility could be a small schema in the tool manifest: "can_be_speculative": true, and an optional "speculative_group" id for sets of interchangeable endpoints. That keeps client contract explicit.

jon: client UX: expose a mode flag on the run call, e.g. `invoke(..., mode="speculative", time_budget_ms=200)` so app teams opt in. fallback to `mode="ordered"` or `mode="confirm"`. We should default to ordered to avoid surprise costs.

maria: agree on opt-in. proposal for server semantics: when speculative group present and mode=speculative, runtime fans out to N compatible backends but adds a low-cost circuit to cancel inflight requests when winner chosen. billing: bill full to the chosen provider, and a smaller reservation/partial charge for speculative attempts? we need legal/pricing sign-off.

vikram: runtime implications: KV cache and stateful tool executions are risky. speculative should be allowed only for idempotent/stateless actions or where tool provides an idempotency token. Also need to guarantee no external side effects double-run. we should require tools to declare idempotency or support compensating actions.

laura: for LLM-driven orchestration, speculative results often differ in quality; we should add result scoring metadata and let the client specify an acceptance predicate, e.g. `min_confidence` or a comparator function. otherwise "first wins" might be lower quality.

maria: launch gating checklist (proposal):
- must have tool manifest fields: can_be_speculative, speculative_group, idempotency_level
- runtime: cancel-on-winner primitives + observability (which candidate won, latencies, costs)
- billing model: spec charges clearly documented + opt-in flag
- SLA: define latency SLOs for speculative mode and a failure-mode for timeouts
- security: ensure auth scopes identical across group members

jon: observability note: console should show per-invoke timeline with speculative arms collapsed by default. we should log: candidates_fired, winner_id, canceled_arms_count, and any partial_costs. Also add an eval hook to capture quality regressions when speculative changes which model output used.

vikram: retries: do we allow ordered retries after speculative budget exhausted? e.g. speculative budget 200ms, then ordered fallback across priority list. That helps availability but increases cost/latency.

maria: yes, staged fallback: speculative -> ordered fast probes -> full ordered. we should make stages configurable per route. add a server-side backoff so we don't overload downstreams.

laura: timeouts: define two timeouts — `speculative_budget_ms` and `hard_timeout_ms`. If no winner by hard_timeout, return error or partial result depending on route. Clients should be able to request a "best-effort partial" that returns the best candidate seen so far.

vikram: API surface example suggestion:
```\nPOST /v1/invoke\n{\n  "tool": "search-v2",\n  "mode": "speculative",\n  "speculative_group": "kb-readers",\n  "speculative_budget_ms": 150,\n  "hard_timeout_ms": 1000,\n  "accept_partial": true\n}\n```\nResponse includes `winner`, `candidates` array (metadata only unless requested), and `billing_summary`.

maria: privacy/security: we must ensure speculative targets don't leak different enterprise scopes. require group members to share identical access scopes or runtime refuses speculative mode.

jon: rollout plan idea:
- alpha: internal + selected partners, speculative only allowed for reading/idempotent ops
- beta: add console metrics and billing transparency
- GA: widen allowed tool classes, add SDK helpers and sample manifests

maria: questions for pricing and legal: do we charge for canceled arms? propose: small "attempt fee" (e.g. 5% of full call) to cover resources, full charge for winner. Need finance input.

vikram: performance engineering: implement early-exit on kernel level and efficient cancel tokens so we reclaim GPU/IO early. also need to measure cold-cache impacts (speculative might worsen cold-cache pressure).

laura: evals: add a regression test that runs speculative vs ordered on representative prompt sets and surfaces any quality deltas.

maria: OK next steps: I'll write a short spec PR with payload examples, manifest changes, and rollout gating. Vikram/Laura/Jon — can you review alpha constraints and runtime requirements by EOD Friday? pinging @vikram @laura @jon :eyes:

deploy-bot: scheduled reminder set for 2025-04-11 09:00 — review speculative invokes alpha constraints.

vikram: ack, will review.

jon: ack, will add console mocks to the PR.

laura: ack, will draft evaluation rubric.

maria: thanks all. :rocket:
